title: 1 Chronicles 22:17–19
context: David commands the leaders of Israel to help Solomon, reminding them that the LORD has given rest on every side. He calls them to set heart and soul on seeking the LORD and to build the sanctuary so the ark and holy vessels can be brought into it. Both traditions read the scene as shared ground on wholehearted devotion and generous preparation for worship.

verses.text: David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
verses.arminianNotes: David commands the princes of Israel to help Solomon. Arminian readers see the work of building God’s house as a shared calling, in which leaders are summoned to support rather than compete with the king.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that David’s preparations extend to the people as well as the materials. The temple will be built by a community joined in purpose, not by one man alone.

verses.text: “Isn’t the LORD your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before the LORD and before his people.
verses.arminianNotes: David reminds the leaders that God has given rest on every side and subdued the land. Arminian readers see past faithfulness as the ground for present obedience, a call to respond gratefully to what God has done.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see rest as God’s gift that frees his people for worship. The subdued land fulfills earlier promises, and the rest becomes the setting for building the house of God.

verses.text: Now set your heart and your soul to follow the LORD your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for the LORD’s name.”
verses.arminianNotes: Set your heart and your soul to follow the LORD your God, then build the sanctuary. Arminian readers note that devotion comes before construction: the building is meant to express a heart already turned to God.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the purpose is to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant into the house, a hope fulfilled in 2 Chronicles 5:7. Worship, not architecture, is the goal of all the preparations.
